verses.text: The LORD said to Moses, "Look, I have made you like God to Pharaoh, and your brother Aaron will be your prophet.
You must say everything I command you, and your brother Aaron will tell Pharaoh to let the people of Israel leave his land.
But I will make Pharaoh stubborn, and I will do many signs and wonders in Egypt.
Pharaoh will not listen to you. Then I will bring my hand down on Egypt, and with great acts of judgment I will bring my people, the people of Israel, out of Egypt, group by group.
The Egyptians will know that I am the LORD when I reach out my hand against Egypt and bring the people of Israel out from among them."
Moses and Aaron did just what the LORD commanded them.
Moses was eighty years old and Aaron was eighty-three when they spoke to Pharaoh.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"When Pharaoh says to you, 'Show me a miracle,' then say to Aaron, 'Take your staff and throw it down in front of Pharaoh,' and it will become a snake."
So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and did just what the LORD commanded. Aaron threw his staff down in front of Pharaoh and his officials, and it became a snake.
Then Pharaoh called for his wise men and sorcerers, and the magicians of Egypt did the same thing with their secret arts.
Each one threw down his staff, and each staff became a snake. But Aaron's staff swallowed up their staffs.
Yet Pharaoh's heart was stubborn, and he would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said.
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Pharaoh's heart is stubborn. He refuses to let the people go.
Go to Pharaoh in the morning, when he goes out to the water. Wait for him on the bank of the Nile. Take in your hand the staff that turned into a snake.
Then say to him, 'The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to say to you: Let my people go, so that they can worship me in the desert. But until now you have not listened.
This is what the LORD says: By this you will know that I am the LORD. With the staff in my hand I will strike the water of the Nile, and it will turn into blood.
The fish in the Nile will die, and the river will stink. The Egyptians will not be able to drink its water.'"

The LORD said to Moses, "Tell Aaron, 'Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt, over its rivers, its streams, its pools, and all its ponds, and they will turn into blood.' There will be blood everywhere in Egypt, even in the wooden buckets and stone jars."
Moses and Aaron did just what the LORD commanded. Aaron raised his staff in front of Pharaoh and his officials and struck the water of the Nile, and all the water in the river turned into blood.
The fish in the Nile died, and the river smelled so bad that the Egyptians could not drink its water. There was blood everywhere in Egypt.
But the magicians of Egypt did the same thing with their secret arts. So Pharaoh's heart stayed stubborn, and he would not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the LORD had said.
Pharaoh turned and went back into his palace, and he did not take even this to heart.
All the Egyptians dug along the Nile to find water to drink, because they could not drink the water of the river.
Seven days passed after the LORD struck the Nile.
